balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Far East Horizon Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Far East Horizon Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Far East Horizon Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Far East Horizon Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Far East Horizon Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

nim.title: Net interest margin & spread
nim.content:
NIM is net interest income (lease and loan interest earned less borrowing cost) as a percentage of interest-earning assets. Net interest spread is the gap between the average yield earned and the average rate paid on borrowings -- the purest read on pricing power, before the leverage effect on NIM.

For Far East Horizon Limited: leasing is a spread business funded mostly by bank borrowings and bonds; FY2025 spread/NIM compression as China's rate cycle fell is the main swing factor in earnings, separate from credit losses.

What to watch:

  • Spread narrowing faster than NIM (funding cost rising relative to lease yield)
  • NIM trend against the PBOC rate cycle

npl.title: Non-performing lease ratio
npl.content:
NPL ratio is the share of the lease and loan book classified non-performing (overdue/impaired), the standard asset-quality gauge for a lender.

For Far East Horizon Limited: this is the single most important risk metric on the page -- a leasing book concentrated in SME and local-government-adjacent customers is more credit-sensitive than a bank's, and NPL drift is the first sign of a problem the P&L has not yet recognised through impairment charges.

What to watch:

  • NPL ratio rising even while NIM holds up (credit cost catching up later)
  • Direction versus China's broader SME credit cycle

costToIncome.title: Cost-to-income ratio
costToIncome.content:
Cost-to-income is operating expenses as a percentage of operating income -- the standard efficiency measure for a lender, parallel to a bank's cost-to-income ratio.

For Far East Horizon Limited: a leasing group with industrial operating segments carries more fixed operating cost (sales teams, asset management, healthcare facilities) than a pure-play lender, so this ratio is the check on whether the industrial diversification is adding operating leverage or just overhead.

What to watch:

  • Ratio rising while NIM/spread compress (double squeeze on earnings)
  • Step changes around new segment investment

industrialOperation.title: Industrial operation revenue
industrialOperation.content:
Industrial operation revenue is the non-leasing segment -- equipment rental and healthcare operations -- Far East Horizon runs alongside its core financial-leasing book.

For Far East Horizon Limited: this segment has grown from roughly 9% of FY2017 revenue to about 37% in FY2025, the company's stated diversification away from pure interest-rate-spread leasing income; FY2025's dip from FY2024 is worth tracking against the leasing book's own growth that year.

What to watch:

  • Industrial revenue share of total revenue, rising or stalling
  • Whether industrial segment margins are disclosed separately and how they compare to the leasing spread

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Far East Horizon Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Far East Horizon Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Far East Horizon Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Far East Horizon Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
